exposure: timing of birth (2-hour intervals, day of the week)
outcome: fetal blood analysis via scalp sampling
admission to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: Uncomplicated first-time mothers who intended vaginal delivery.
finding: Specific timepoints and days of the week were associated with increased laboratory signs of fetal distress (e.g., lower umbilical pH on Friday afternoons, lower base excess on Sunday mornings), but these did not translate into an increased rate of severe asphyxia or worse 5-min Apgar scores, while fetal blood analysis via scalp sampling was performed less frequently on weekends.
mod_finding: The distribution of the mode of delivery did not differ across the investigated time periods.
